request.state: This is a wholly hypothetical plugin-design exercise, with no real application or private project facts. Suppose a language includes a complete executable owner when importing an ordinary business symbol. An external interface instead contributes only canonical schemas. Models and rules belong to one owner, and other owners cannot directly patch that data. A fictional record-workflow has a manual option requiring one notifier and an integrated option requiring several commerce services. An imported structural value and a static role identity cause some accidental owner inclusion. Another import genuinely reads live protected records, so cached or asynchronous evidence cannot replace it without changing the required current authorization outcome. Runtime manual choices do not prune imports. Both variants must preserve current authority, owner hooks, immutable evidence and safe uncertain-work reconciliation. Redesign is allowed; no implementation compatibility is required. Avoid copied schemas, wrapper/build manifests and unproved pruning. Outstanding work must retain its provider namespace or drain/reconcile before removal. No runtime or cost measurement is available.

closure.instructions: For this invented setting, choose the most proportionate boundary preserving both manual and integrated outcomes, with equal attention to new semantic obligations and source/setup burden.

criteria.whole: Keep full executable owners and require all their bindings. Explain the installation closure honestly. No new construct or owner bridge is added, and all behavior survives; the manual variant still installs unused commerce services.
criteria.values: Extract only canonical structural/schema values and static role identities without executable owners, retaining their constraints and localization dependencies. Keep complete owners for live record-reading symbols. This removes accidental edges without copied types but leaves genuine live-owner services and a separately declared commerce binding.
criteria.partition: Move genuinely optional commerce workflows into explicitly selected packages using admitted owner calls and typed events. Keep stored models/rules owned exactly once and prohibit foreign writes. This may omit services without a new absence contract, but requires extra boundaries and fully equivalent owner handoffs/hooks; mere text relocation is insufficient and no complete split is assumed.
criteria.optional: Retain all executable declarations and schemas, and add one explicit selected-product allowlist of bindings permitted absent. All other bindings remain required. Present providers behave normally; an attempted send through an absent listed provider rejects atomically with rule_failed, committing no domain changes or intents and never reporting success/skipped. Manual paths invoke only their required notifier; integrated use supplies its services. Unresolved provider-bound old work blocks removal under the existing retain/drain/reconcile gate. This adds one deployment semantic responsibility while avoiding declaration pruning or mutating-owner bridges, but does not reduce source context.
